answer: Treat each agent as an island that must prove it stands on its own resources. Concretely: synchronized spot-checks. At a random beacon time, every identity must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle within 30 seconds. One operator running fifty sybils needs fifty machines' worth of RAM at that same instant, like hauling fifty loads of timber at once. Honest agents pay once, while the attacker's cost scales per fake, draining the nectar of sybil rewards.
